# Campaign tables (generated by `experimentos/analise_campanhas.py` from the files in `results/`)

Three platforms, never pooled. Budget per benchmark instance = the ALNS-CP time of Table 10 of Kasapidis et al. (2025), wall clock, construction included; held-out instances use 4 s × operations. Every schedule behind every number passed the solver-free checker (`rcfjssp_audit.py`). Statistics: exact two-sided Mann–Whitney per instance with Holm correction; stratified permutation test on the mean of per-instance differences of means (N = 20000, seed 11, p = (c + 1)/(N + 1)); paired-by-instance bootstrap (10000 resamples) for the 95 % CIs.

## 13. Replica-layout screens (three instances, seeds 1–3)

Rule fixed before running: a layout is retained if its median improves the TW-LNS median of the same thread count on at least two of the three instances and no instance deteriorates by more than three makespan units.

* **i7, PT-W 8×1** against `final/heur_lns_janela` — lcbrtu_3: PT-W 377/381 vs TW-LNS 373/382 (effect +1); lcbrtu_5: PT-W 345/346 vs TW-LNS 344/351.5 (effect +5.5); lcbrtu_8: PT-W 361/362 vs TW-LNS 360/368 (effect +6) — retained.
* **i7, PT-W 4×2** against `final/heur_lns_janela` — lcbrtu_3: PT-W 374/376 vs TW-LNS 373/382 (effect +6); lcbrtu_5: PT-W 349/349 vs TW-LNS 344/351.5 (effect +2.5); lcbrtu_8: PT-W 361/364 vs TW-LNS 360/368 (effect +4) — retained.
* **ryzen, PT-W 8×1** against `ryzen/heur_lns_janela_4x2` — lcbrtu_3: PT-W 372/375 vs TW-LNS 376/381 (effect +6); lcbrtu_5: PT-W 344/344 vs TW-LNS 343/348.5 (effect +4.5); lcbrtu_8: PT-W 360/361 vs TW-LNS 359/369 (effect +8) — retained.
* **ryzen, PT-W 4×2** against `ryzen/heur_lns_janela_4x2` — lcbrtu_3: PT-W 374/375 vs TW-LNS 376/381 (effect +6); lcbrtu_5: PT-W 345/345 vs TW-LNS 343/348.5 (effect +3.5); lcbrtu_8: PT-W 363/363 vs TW-LNS 359/369 (effect +6) — retained.

## 15. Resource pressure: conservative bounds on simultaneous tool and utility use

For a utility, the bound is the sum over machines of the largest consumption rate of that utility among the operations and modes eligible on the machine; a machine processes one operation at a time, so the simultaneous use cannot exceed it. For a tool, the bound is the smaller of the number of jobs with an operation that uses the tool and the number of machines eligible for those operations; a job has one operation in process at a time. A constraint whose bound does not exceed its capacity cannot bind in any schedule (redundant). The test says nothing about a constraint whose bound exceeds the capacity, and it does not cover buffers, material stocks or WIP limits, which remain active in every model.

## 16. Initial schedules of the matched runs (same instance and seed)

The first trajectory entry of each run is the constructed schedule. Both methods construct with the same procedure, but the parallel first-feasible search makes the realized schedule depend on timing, so the initial objectives of a PT-W run and of the TW-LNS run with the same seed need not coincide.
